title: Splitting and reaping: dividing infinite subsets of omega
summary: Two uncountable minima measure how many subsets are needed to split every infinite set or resist every common splitter.
abstract: The even numbers divide the natural numbers into two infinite pieces, but cannot divide the even numbers themselves this way. A set splits an infinite set when it leaves infinitely many points on each side. Every countable family of infinite sets has a common splitter, while no countable collection of splitters handles all infinite sets. The splitting number measures the smallest family that splits every infinite set; the reaping number measures the smallest family with no common splitter.
